title: On‑Prem vs VPC — Capacity Sizing and Support Matrix
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to align on capacity sizing assumptions and map support/licensing bundles to realistic 3‑year TCOs for customer RFPs (on‑prem vs VPC). This is intentionally concise — use as the source for pricing guidance for sales engineering and to surface open tradeoffs for product.

Topline summary (short):
- For steady, high utilization (>70%) and long refresh cycles (3+ years), on‑prem CAPEX can beat VPC in raw infra cost but only if customer accepts >1.5x ops staffing and spare-capacity risk.
- For spiky workloads, VPC with reserved + burst is generally cheaper and simpler operationally.
- Support bundle level is a major lever: adding 24/7 SLA + on‑call (Gold/Platinum) can double the yearly support line on small deployments and flip economics to VPC.

Key scenarios modeled (tabs implied):
A) Small steady (100 QPS peak, 5 qps avg, 2k tokens/request)
B) Medium growth (500 QPS peak, 25 qps avg)
C) Large enterprise (2k QPS peak, 100 qps avg, multi-region)

Assumptions (editable):
- Token profile: avg 2k tokens per request; tail 5k tokens for 5% requests.
- Model: 13B dense; perf: 25 tokens/sec per GPU (post-optimizations); KV cache hit reduces avg tokens/sec per request by ~10%
- Hardware SKU (on‑prem): 8x A100 80GB equiv per rack; list unit cost $320k per rack (incl power distribution, 3yr warranty), refresh=3 yr amortization
- VPC SKU: rtx-a100-80 equivalent 1 GPU hourly price (on commit) $2.50/hr -> $2,000/month reserved (example)
- Networking egress: VPC egress $0.09/GB (estimate) vs on‑prem: carrier/MPLS cost amortized per month
- Staffing: Sysadmin + MLE ops: on‑prem baseline 1.75 FTE per 10 racks; VPC ops 0.6 FTE per similar capacity (automation savings)
- Support bundles: Bronze (business hours, 48h response) 6% ARR; Silver (24/7, 4h) 12% ARR; Gold (24/7 + on-site quarterly + priority) 25% ARR. These are starting points; discounts apply for multi-year.

Sheet excerpt: Cost line items (annualized, USD) — example for Medium scenario (3‑year window):
Columns: CostItem | OnPrem-Year1 | OnPrem-Year2 | OnPrem-Year3 | VPC-Year1 | VPC-Year2 | VPC-Year3
Rows:
- Hardware CAPEX (amortized) | 420,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0
- Infra OPEX (power, colocation) | 120,000 | 124,000 | 128,000 | 0 | 0 | 0
- Network (WAN/MPLS) | 36,000 | 36,900 | 37,800 | 5,400 | 5,600 | 5,800
- Licensing (platform) | 96,000 | 96,000 | 96,000 | 96,000 | 96,000 | 96,000
- Support (Silver @12% ARR on license) | 11,520 | 11,520 | 11,520 | 11,520 | 11,520 | 11,520
- Staff (ops, infra) | 210,000 | 216,000 | 222,000 | 72,000 | 74,000 | 76,000
- Cloud compute (reserved + burst) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 340,000 | 352,000 | 365,000
- Misc (refresh spare parts, travel, compliance) | 12,000 | 12,500 | 13,000 | 4,000 | 4,200 | 4,400
= Total annual | 895,520 | 460,920 | 488,320 | 528,920 | 543,320 | 558,720

Notes on the numbers: these are illustrative; primary drivers are hardware utilization and cloud commit discount. OnPrem front-loads cost (Year1 big), VPC more level. Break-even tends to occur in year 2–3 if utilization >75% and hardware refresh cost declines by >10% from our procurement.

Support bundle analysis (impact on TCO):
- Example: switching from Silver -> Gold for Medium scenario increases support line from 11.5k to 24k/year — on small deals this can add >10% to annual spend and push customers to VPC option. Recommend offering a ‘Gold-lite’ 2x Silver (18% ARR) for 3yr prescriptive deployments to hit middle ground.

Sensitivity quick-check (editable knobs):
- Utilization +/- 10% -> TCO delta (onprem) +/- 18% over 3yr
- Cloud commit discount (1yr vs 3yr) change from 35% -> 50% -> shifts VPC favorability strongly
- Support % of ARR: threshold ~18% where onprem advantage disappears for medium/low scale

Capacity sizing matrix (decision heuristics):
- If avg utilization > 60% and expected growth predictable -> prefer on‑prem if customer can accept 3yr commit & manage ops.
- If multi-region low-latency or bursty unpredictable load -> prefer VPC (regional routing + reserved pools + auto-fallback)

Bundle recommendations for Sales Engineering (draft):
- Small deal (<$500k 3yr spend): recommend VPC + Silver; avoid Gold unless paid uplift
- Mid deal ($500k–$2M 3yr): offer OnPrem starter bundle (1 rack + Silver + 1 proserv day) with 10% multi-year discount, and VPC reserved with 2yr commit as alternative
- Large enterprise (>$2M 3yr): Custom pricing, include Platinum support option with prioritized capacity, DR runbooks, and 24/7 SRE access. Consider hybrid: primary on‑prem + VPC for disaster + surge.

- When selling onprem, package 1yr SRE retainer at reduced hourly to mitigate staffing objections.
